SPELLTHRONE

Two archmages. One floating island. The throne is listening.

Spellthrone v3.38 · Slice 3.38 — Courts & Longevity — nine pieces a side on a wider isle: two great mages, Guardians who step in, fires that spread and frosts that root, and a Deepening at Round 7. A piece still to act wears a ring of light; once it has acted, the ring is gone and the piece rests dimmer. Orbit low and the island’s under-rock is lit from below now, mana seams glowing in the dark. The court breathes: pieces idle on their own time, rise when chosen, and flash when struck. And the Exclusives are serpents now — Ember's Cinderwyrm and Frost's Rimewyrm coil where the hounds once ran, forked tongues and all — while the archers stand in a true shooter's stance, arrows level. And the air itself has taken sides: embers rise over Ember's half of the isle while snow sifts down over Frost's, the braziers' firelight dances with their own flames, and gold, ice and plate catch real reflections of the dusk. The camera has learned manners too: four preset views fly you smoothly around the court, and left alone it breathes, very slowly, like something alive. On the board, pieces travel like they mean it now: moves glide hex to hex on an eased arc, strikes lunge and recoil, and the fallen shrink into their burst of court-colored sparks. And the wyrms themselves have been taken down a size — a small trim, so the serpents coil beside the band instead of towering over it. And the board itself has been polished to the pieces’ shine — the Dusk Slate now catches the same dusk as the gold and ice it carries. And the island no longer floats in front of a poster: a ruined colonnade rings the sky, mist pools below the rock, and the horizon glows warm toward Ember and cool toward Frost. And the Heart Crystals have woken: a Sprite that ends its activation kneeling on its own crystal and lives to stir again rises as a True Spirit — Inferno or Hearth for Ember, Blizzard or Glacier Wisp for Frost — and the kneeling wears a ring of light the whole board can read, so the race to stop it is fair. And the tutorial itself has been walked end to end, exactly as written, by a tireless first student: its gold ring now points at the Cinderbow who can actually loose the lesson's arrows, and the no-dice lesson waits for a strike of your own before it shows you the arithmetic. And the Waking itself can now be watched: when a Communion completes, the Sprite rises and turns in its court's light, the ring's sparks fall inward, and at the flash the piece on the board is the Spirit itself — Inferno and Hearth wear the Coal Imp's fire grown wild and warm, Blizzard and Glacier Wisp wear the Veil Wisp's mist grown storm and still: four new faces for the two forks of each court. And the spellbook itself has been slimmed: seventeen spells are twelve now, each a different verb — the High Mage has become the support mage, carrying Blink and Mend and the court's Resonance in her own hands (lose her, and you lose Resonance and her utility both), Ember has learned to set the very ground ablaze for a round, and Frost's Brittle has become Shatter, which only breaks what the cold already holds. And the tuning fork has come home: after a night of thousands of measured games on a fork of this very build, the Archmage stands at 17 HP, Fireball and Shatter cost ◆4 apiece, the Deepening holds its breath until Round 7, and the Throne starts paying a round later — the same duel, given room to breathe, with the balance confirmed rather than disturbed. And the hand itself has been trued: a tap now lands where the finger came DOWN, not where it lifted — the board holds still from the moment you touch it, so the hex at a border takes the order you aimed at it. And two seats have become one: the Court view and the Player view were near-twins, so a single seat remains — behind your own court against the machine, and in a pass-and-play duel it settles behind whoever is to move, a touch higher and closer, the way the Player view always sat. And the court has been grounded: every piece now stands in a soft pool of its own shade, so serpent and plate alike sit planted on the slate instead of hovering over it; the ruins have crept closer — broken drums and capital stones hang in a nearer ring beyond the rim, below the board’s edge where no sightline to a hex can cross them; and the hero lights burn hotter — brazier flame, heart crystal and wyrm-seam raised toward the studio band — while the slate beneath them keeps its dusk. And the turning hand keeps what it turns: the camera rides the steering finger exactly, so a fast swing stops dead the moment the hand lets go — no trailing settle behind it, and nothing left for the next touch to snap shut. And the camera has learned to land like a living thing: a hard swing now spends its last momentum in a short gliding settle — every frame of it continuous, never a jump — and a fresh touch simply stops the board where it lies, so the hex under your finger is always the hex you aimed at. And the view cluster has shed its two oldest buttons — Top view and Reset view are gone, because the preset row already says it all: Overhead is the top view, Court is the home seat — while the Terrain legend keeps its place. And the King has learned to step sideways: the Archmage now carries Blink ◆3 — vanish and reappear on an empty hex within 3, himself only, priced like the escape it is (◆2 from a Mana Font) — while the Queen keeps her cheaper ◆2 step, her Mend and her Resonance: lose her, and you lose the court's utility still. And beneath the duel a stage has been built — hand-set scenes, scripted volleys answered by real Guardians, a camera that flies to the lesson, and gates that hold every tap but the one being taught; the new way in will be staged on it, beat by beat. And the stage has its first lesson now — the Font: a hurt Archmage stands in the discount with two hill bows holding his life in their hands (3 + 3 against his 5), spends the Font's price break twice — a ◆3 Fireball, then a ◆2 Blink to the far hex his Guards flank — and the wyrm and the bow come for him anyway, 3 and 2, exactly his life again, and each of his Pyre Guards answers for him once. Scene 1 stands open in the menu: 'Scene 1 — The Font'. And four more lessons have taken the stage: the Queen — six hexes from her dying king, one Blink from Mend range, her mana counted to the last point (◆2, ◆2, ◆5) so the Resonance lands and the wyrm's killing 4 meets a mended 5; the Triangle — a needle that kills only because Scouts hunt bows (1 + 1 into 2), a pin that costs a Bulwark his one job, and a strike that lands on a queen because her Guardian cannot stand; Kindling — a blade of 3 made 4 against a life of exactly 4, and a Sprite whose death is itself a weapon; and the Long Way — a Guard on the Throne through three rounds of weather (10, 8, 6), the crown ticking 1, 2, 3, a duel won without a kill. The stage also keeps its own house now: the hint banner is recomputed at every beat, so it can never invite a move the moment refuses. Scenes 1–5 stand open in the menu. And the board now answers when you ask it: tap any enemy and its reach blooms over the slate — the deep red it can strike from where it stands, the pale red it could only reach by moving first — priced by the same movement and targeting the duel itself obeys, so the shading can no more lie than the AI can. Tap it again, tap the ground, or choose one of your own pieces to let it go; and no tap that means an attack or a spell is ever spent on looking. And the stage has learned to greet: a player who has never dueled is walked onto it as the island first rises — the Font, the Queen, the Triangle, the Kindling, the Long Way, one lesson handing them to the next — and at the end of the Long Way the stage does not close: the board beneath it becomes a real one, the camera pulls back to the Court seat in a single flight, and the first move of a real duel is already theirs. Leave at any point and the island remembers — it never drags anyone back; the lessons wait in the menu, where they have always waited. And the lessons have been walked blind: a stranger who knew nothing — reading only the coach's words, the gold ring, and the glow of what may be tapped — found every tap in every scene, from the menu and from the first-launch chain alike, and at the end of the Long Way took the first move of a real duel for his own. Every wrong thing he tried along the way was answered kindly — the enemy who blooms red when looked at and lets go when the ground is tapped, the End that refuses, the wrong march and the wrong Blink the stage rewinds and forgives — though the walking caught one real trap and mended it: a finished beat's buttons used to sit live into the next, a leftover Confirm waiting to be tapped into a plan with nowhere to go; now the card clears when its selection does, and the stage sweeps its own card clean at every beat. The menu has tidied itself too, at the word of the house: the five lessons fold under one 📚 Lessons door beneath the Tutorial, so the front page is short again — and every lesson still stands there for the replaying. The stage's door has moved, too: 'Leave the stage' no longer sits in the coach's row beside the way forward — it lives on a small ✕ Leave chip in the menu's corner, one tap to ask 'Sure?', a second to go, the house rule the old Skip taught; and the camera's three seats have quieted themselves — ghost-pale and small at rest, waking only when a hand comes near, their poses unchanged. And the top of the screen has been put in order: the Terrain key, the camera's three seats, and — while a lesson stands — the stage's ✕ door now share ONE slim row under the banner, where there used to be a stack of rows; the seats keep their ghost and their poses, the door keeps its two-tap 'Sure?', and nothing else up there moved. Learn it in a minute. Master it in a season.

CHOOSE YOUR COURT

HOW TO PLAY

The duel. You command an Archmage, a High Mage and seven followers on a wide hex island. Players alternate activating one piece per turn — move, then strike or cast (or stay and act). When every piece has acted the round ends: crowns are counted, mana flows, everyone refreshes. Combat never rolls dice — the numbers are always exactly what you see. Mastery is positioning.

🏆 Two ways to win. Slay the enemy Archmage — or hold the golden Throne at the island's heart: end a round as its sole holder, three times. Crowns are counted from Round 4 — the first three rounds belong to the armies. If 24 rounds pass with no victor, the crowns decide; tied crowns fall to the stronger warband.

YOUR WARBAND

🔮 Archmage 17 HP
Casts the court's book, bolts foes for 2 at range 2–3, and carries 🔮 Blink ◆3 — he steps sideways himself, and only himself. If he falls, you lose.
👑 High Mage 8 HP
The queen — the court's support mage: 🔮 Blink, 💚 Mend, and the court's Resonance spell are hers to cast, plus a bolt at range 2–4. Resonance answers only while both great mages stand — and she alone casts it. Lose the queen and you lose Resonance and her utility both — not the duel.
🗿 Guardian 10–11 HP
A walking wall. Hits for 3 in melee; allies beside one take −1 damage; and once a round a Guardian can Intercept — take a hit meant for a neighbor (the defender chooses, seeing the damage). Ember's Pyre Guard bites back for 1; Frost's Bulwark (11 HP) chills whatever strikes it or its aura.
🏹 Skirmisher 5 HP
Shoots for 2 at range 2–3, never point-blank. Ember's Cinderbow primes Burning and, standing still, looses a Volley at a second foe; Frost's Shardbow chills — and standing still, its shot drives the cold deeper: a foe already Chilled is Rooted where they stand (Still Aim). A fresh foe is only Chilled.
🧚 Scout 5 HP
Flits 4 hexes through forests as if they were air; stings for 1 and needles at range 2. Ember's Spark Sprite bursts on death; Frost's Mist Sprite, in a forest, cannot be targeted by ranged fire beyond 2 hexes while no enemy stands adjacent. And the Scout alone can make the Pilgrimage — end an activation on her own court's Heart Crystal, survive to her next, and she wakes as a True Spirit.
🕯️ Enabler 6 HP
Points outward, never heals. Ember's Kindlebrand lights an ally's next attack (+1, primes Burning); Frost's Rimewarden wraps an ally in ice — the Ward: the next hit they take is negated. But great mages burn too bright to hold a ward, so no Archmage or High Mage may be warded.
🐍 Court Exclusive 6–7 HP
Ember's Cinderwyrm: a coiled serpent of stone plate and magma — fast, +1 vs Burning prey, runs farther toward fire. Frost's Rimewyrm: a serpent of ice plate over glacier light — its hits chill, +1 vs Chilled, +1 more vs Rooted.
▲ The triangle
Classes circle: Scout +1 dmg vs Skirmisher · Guardian +1 dmg vs Scout · Skirmisher pins Guardians (a pinned Guardian cannot Intercept that round; his aura never sleeps). Bonus-only — the favored hit wears a ▲ on the target's number.

THE GROUND

Hill (raised, rocky) — striking FROM a hill: +1 damage
Forest (trees) — −1 damage taken standing in it · costs 2 movement to enter (Scouts ignore the cost)
Mana Font (violet crystals) — a great mage standing here gains +1 extra mana each round, on top of the usual +1 — and spells cast while standing on one cost ◆1 less (never below ◆1). Fonts are casting platforms: the spell buttons show the font price while a caster stands there. Six fonts: a home pair per court, and a contested pair on the rims.
Throne (gold, center) — end a round as its sole holder, 3 times, to win · crowns count from Round 4
Heart Crystal — deep in each home burns the enemy element's crystal. The Pilgrimage: your Scout seeks ITS OWN court's crystal, the one waiting in the enemy home. End its activation standing on it and the Communion begins — a turning ring of light around the kneeling Sprite is the whole board's warning. If it still stands there at the start of its next activation, it wakes as a True Spirit (8 HP · Move 3 · strikes for 3, no spells) and you pick its form on the spot: Ember chooses 🔥 Inferno (its touch sets foes Burning; its death-burst doubles) or 🏮 Hearth (Burning foes beside it tick for 2); Frost chooses ❄️ Blizzard (foes starting beside it are Chilled) or 🌨️ Glacier Wisp (Mistveil everywhere — no forest needed; foes at range 2, or beside it, still reach it). Death is the only interruption — damage alone never breaks the Communion. Guard the ground around yours.

SPELLS — THE GREAT MAGES CAST

Ember's book (the Archmage casts): 🔥 Fireball ◆4 (3 to a hex, 1 around it — and survivors catch Burning, friends included) · 🎇 Ignite ◆2 (every Burning enemy takes its Burning tick NOW) · 🌋 Wildfire ◆4 (set a hex ablaze for the rest of the round: 2 to whoever stands on it, and everything within 1 hex — friend or foe — catches Burning) · 💚 Mend ◆2 · 🔮 Blink ◆3 (the Archmage steps sideways — vanish and reappear on an empty hex within 3; himself only, and dearer than the Queen's ◆2 step).

Frost's book (the Archmage casts): 🧊 Frost Lance ◆2 (2 damage + Chill) · 🔨 Shatter ◆4 (4 damage to a Chilled or Rooted foe, and its Chill is spent — it can only break what the cold already holds) · 🏔️ Glacier ◆4 (an ice wall: blocks movement, 2 rounds) · 💚 Mend ◆2 · 🔮 Blink ◆3 (the Archmage steps sideways — vanish and reappear on an empty hex within 3; himself only, and dearer than the Queen's ◆2 step).

The High Mage is the support mage: 🔮 Blink ◆2 (vanish and reappear on an empty hex within 3) · 💚 Mend ◆2 — and the court's Resonance spell is hers alone to cast, only while both great mages live: Ember — ☄️ Conflagration ◆5. Frost — 🥶 Deep Freeze ◆5 (every enemy Chilled; the already-Chilled crack for 3 and come out Rooted).

Signatures (once per game, sealed until the Deepening at Round 7): 🌠 Meteor ◆5 (Ember) · 🌡️ Absolute Zero ◆6 (Frost).

Burning & Chill. Every Ember attack primes Burning: 1 damage at the start of the burning piece's own activation; marks fade at round's end. Every Frost attack applies Chill: −1 movement on the victim's next activation; 2 Chill means Rooted — no movement at all. Neither ever stuns.

Spells ignore hills, woods and auras — raw magic answers to nothing (but a Rimewarden's ward eats any single hit, spell or steel). Mana: you start with ◆3 and gain +1 each round (+1 more with your Archmage on a Mana Font, +1 more after the Deepening), up to ◆8. Casting from a Mana Font costs ◆1 less (minimum ◆1).

That is the whole game. The rest — tempo, traps, throne pressure, when to bank mana and when to burn it — is the mastery. New here? The 🎓 Tutorial on the menu teaches all of it at the board.
